summary: TraumaTeam is an astronaut health monitoring platform powered by real hardware, not simulated data. By uniting a Zepp OS smartwatch, Bluetooth smart scale, hands-free bilingual voice mobile app, interactive 3D body mapper, and flight surgeon web console, it tracks live vitals, body composition, injury photos, and gamified daily check-ins across five mission environments. Built for deep-space missions with delayed ground support, it triggers automated alerts and delivers verified aerospace medicine guidance. This empowers crews to detect physiological changes early, lower cognitive overload, and protect astronaut health from Earth to Space.
details:
Hackamoles Returns' Project Solution

TraumaTeam bridges the gap between raw consumer/wearable hardware and spaceflight clinical decision-making. Instead of forcing astronauts to cross-reference disconnected spreadsheets, PDF manuals, and isolated sensors, TraumaTeam unifies continuous physiological telemetry, self-reported symptoms, body composition tracking, countermeasure habits, and peer-reviewed space medicine into four connected layers:

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]

How Does Our Solution Work?

Rather than generating synthetic demo curves, TraumaTeam captures real measurements from physical hardware:

  • Smartwatch with a  background App Service polls real heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, stress score, daily steps, and sleep duration. Telemetry routes over Bluetooth LE via the phone’s Zepp Side Service proxy to a serverless ingestion API and PostgreSQL database, backed by a persistent minute-level recovery watchdog so accidental service stops restart automatically.
  • Connected Smart Scale that captures real weight readings over BLE advertisements and sends them securely to the backend. From weight and the crew member’s profile (height, age, and sex), the backend computes exact WHO BMI classifications and ideal-weight bands, alongside transparently labeled population-based estimates for body fat %, body water %, lean mass, and basal metabolism.

2. Mission-Adaptive Environment & Daily Routines (Mobile Companion)

On TraumaTeam Mobile, the interface adapts visually and operationally across five mission regimes:

  • Earth (1.0g Base)
  • In Spaceship (Orbit / 0g Microgravity)
  • Space Station (0g Microgravity)
  • Lunar Base (0.16g Lunar Gravity)
  • Mars Surface (0.38g Martian Gravity)

Astronauts track their live heart-rate waveform, oxygenation, stress, sleep history, and Earth-to-Mars mission progress alongside gamified daily missions and Duolingo-style streaks (hydration, exercise routines, and daily health check-ins for mood, symptoms, and optional manual glucose, blood pressure, or body temperature).

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]

3. Interactive 3D Anatomical Mapping & Longitudinal Injury Tracking

In both mobile and web views, an interactive Three.js 3D musculoskeletal model lets users rotate, zoom, and tap 36 specific body zones (such as the rotator cuff, lumbar spine, or quadriceps).

  • Color-coded severity heatmap (Mild 1 → Moderate 5 → Intense 10) shows active musculoskeletal pain, swelling, and functional limitation at a glance.
  • Injury Photo Dossier: Crew members can attach timestamped sequence photos to any muscle zone (stored privately via signed URLs) to visually inspect bruising, skin changes, or healing progression over time.
[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]

4. Hands-Free Bilingual Voice Control (EN / ES)

When astronauts are inside EVA gear, exercising on a treadmill, or unable to type, TraumaTeam Voice provides hands-free navigation, check-in dictation, vitals readouts, alert acknowledgements, and symptom logging in English and Spanish.

  • An offline natural-language parser executes common commands immediately using native OS speech recognition and spoken feedback.
  • Unrecognized phrasing optionally routes through the backend and is strictly rebuilt against a server-side intent whitelist  so ungrounded or unexpected model outputs are discarded.

5. Flight Surgeon Console, Automated Alerts & Citation-Verified RAG

On TraumaTeam Web (React 19 + Vite), ground flight surgeons and onboard CMOs monitor crew health from a dedicated desktop/tablet/mobile console featuring a live ECG canvas, smart-scale body composition carousel, muscle update history, and an automated Alerts Inbox:

  • Database-Level Clinical Rules: PostgreSQL transaction triggers automatically raise a Critical alert if any active injury reaches pain ≥ 8/10, and a Warning alert when an astronaut accumulates ≥ 4 concurrent active conditions—maintaining separate read states for the astronaut and ground medical team.
  • Zero-Hallucination Evidence Assistant (RAG): To avoid unsafe invented medical advice, TraumaTeam indexes 17 curated aerospace-medicine sources 5 official NASA & Canadian Space Agency (CSA) spaceflight health snapshots and 12 curated peer-reviewed research evidence summaries (covering lumbar muscle atrophy, EVA shoulder mechanics, NASA SPRINT exercise countermeasures, bone recovery, wearable SpO₂ limits, HRV stress, circadian misalignment, partial gravity, thermoregulation, sensorimotor readaptation, and Artemis radiation).
  • Local BM25 retrieval fetches the highest-matching passages first. When optional DeepSeek explanation synthesis is enabled, the backend validates every returned [citation] ID and source URL against the curated catalog; if no specific study applies or generation is off/unavailable, the system openly switches to evidence_only or insufficient_evidence instead of guessing a diagnosis.

Who Benefits from TraumaTeam?

  • Astronauts & Crew Medical Officers: Replaces scattered trackers and static PDF guides with one fast visual check-in, hands-free voice logging, and mission-routine engagement.
  • Flight Surgeons & Mission Control: Delivers synchronized telemetry, pain-severity heatmaps, longitudinal recovery photos, and auditable source citations—even when Earth communication drops.
  • Terrestrial Isolated & Remote Care: The same offline-resilient wearable pipeline, 3D anatomical symptom mapper, and voice-first UX directly translate to polar research bases, maritime crews, rural/remote telemedicine, physical rehabilitation, and elder care.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • Wearable & Hardware Integration with  Zepp OS App Service & Side Service, Bluetooth Low Energy smart scale decoding, Vercel serverless ingestion APIs.
  • Mobile Companion with TypeScript, Expo SDK 58, React Native, Expo Router, NativeWind, Three.js (3D body viewer), Lottie animations, expo-speech-recognition & expo-speech.
  • Flight Surgeon Web Console: React 19, Vite, TypeScript, CSS View Transitions, Three.js interactive WebGL anatomy viewer, HTML5 60Hz ECG canvas.
  • Backend, Alerts & Database: NestJS 11, TypeScript, Supabase PostgreSQL (10 SQL migrations, Row Level Security, transactional PL/pgSQL alert triggers, PGlite SQL verification tests), signed Supabase Storage image URLs.
  • AI & Scientific Knowledge Sources: Local BM25 retrieval (23 indexed passages across 5 official NASA / CSA spaceflight health resources and 12 curated peer-reviewed aerospace medicine summaries), optional DeepSeek API synthesis.
